topic: Triathlon Training App Stamina Raises $2M, Backed by Olympic Champion

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Triathlon Training App Stamina Raises $2M, Backed by Olympic Champion

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Athletech News

facts.label: Deal
facts.value: raise $2M

facts.label: Article
facts.value: The London-based startup has surpassed 50,000 downloads since launching in 2025, offering personalized training plans for endurance athletes London-based triathlon training app Stamina has raised $2 million in seed funding, with backing from Olympic cycling champion Greg Van Avermaet, as it looks to make personalized coaching more accessible to endurance athletes. The round also included investments from Belgian funds Syndicate One and 100IN, content creator Average Rob and former professional basketball player Tomas Van Den Spiegel, among other investors. Founded by Willem Duyck and Shuowang He, Stamina creates personalized training plans that combine swimming, cycling and running, adjusting workouts based on an athlete’s fitness level, available time and race goals. Stamina was born out of Duyck’s experience preparing for his first half-distance triathlon in 2023, when he found himself choosing between expensive personal coaching and generic training plans that couldn’t adapt to his schedule. Unlike fitness apps that use generative AI to create workouts, Stamina relies on a proprietary training algorithm developed alongside coaches and professional triathletes Ari Klau and Greg Harper. “Ask an AI chatbot for a training plan twice and you’ll often get two different answers,” He said. “That’s fine for writing an email, but not for your training.

facts.value: For her. What’s happening: The wellness technology company acquired IP from Embr Labs, maker of a thermoregulating wearable for menopausal women, with plans for new women’s devices. Cool it. Tackling hot flashes and sleep issues, Embr ’s Wave wearable delivers precision heating and cooling at the wrist, with AI sensing capable of predicting 82% of events in as little as 17 seconds before they happen. The MIT spinout has sold nearly 250K devices to date. Re-up. Doubling down on its women’s initiative launched in 2025, Therabody will add the thermal technology and research into its expanding performance, beauty , and thermoregulation portfolio — which already includes PowerDot, its TENS device featuring a period pain mode. Femtech 2.0. Finally getting the attention it deserves, menopause is on wellness’s agenda, with wearable features and digital support emerging daily. But now, tech makers are shifting from monitoring to real-time modification, with Samphire Neuro and OhmBody pioneering stim devices and Eight Sleep launching menopause mode. Punchline: A natural extension for Therabody, Embr’s IP strengthens its commitment to helping women look, feel, and perform their best at all stages of life. topic: Ditching the “Fat Scanner” Label to Boost Retention and Revenue with Ashley Ziegler Henzler of seca

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Ditching the “Fat Scanner” Label to Boost Retention and Revenue with Ashley Ziegler Henzler of seca

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Club Solutions

facts.label: Article
facts.value: A body composition scanner sitting on the club floor isn’t a strategy. The operators who profit from the technology treat each scan as the start of a member relationship, not a one-time assessment. Ashley Ziegler Henzler, the senior sales manager at seca, argues that clubs with wearable-literate, GLP-1 curious members must move the conversation beyond weight and body fat or risk losing those members to apps and AI chatbots that will interpret their results instead. Ziegler Henzler joined Club Solutions Magazine editor and podcast host Taylor Gabhart to discuss how operators can reposition body composition as a health analyzer rather than a “fat scanner,” which metrics matter most, and how to build a scanning culture that drives engagement and retention. She also covers the role of body composition tracking for members on GLP-1s and the scan days, challenges and front desk practices that club can launch ahead of the new year. topic: McKinsey Values Wellness at $2.7T, but Says Key Markets Are Underserved

facts.label: Story
facts.value: McKinsey Values Wellness at $2.7T, but Says Key Markets Are Underserved

facts.label: Outlet
facts.value: Athletech News

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Wellness brands are growing twice as fast as the rest of consumer goods, yet 4 in 10 consumers say the market still isn’t delivering what they want most Wellness now ranks second only to family on consumers’ priority lists, ahead of career and friendships. What’s no secret: the money has followed. According to McKinsey & Company’s fifth Future of Wellness report, the U.S. wellness market alone tops $700 billion and is growing 5% to 10% a year. McKinsey valued the total wellness market at $2.7 billion (the Global Wellness Institute, by contrast, estimates the wellness economy is worth $7.5 trillion. ) And yet consumers still aren’t fully satisfied. The management consulting firm surveyed more than 10,000 consumers in China, Germany, the U.K. and the U.S., and roughly 40% said today’s offerings fall short on longevity, mental health and mobility. It’s a complaint that hasn’t been resolved since 2024, and depending on how you look at it, it’s also an opportunity. The problem isn’t a lack of products. Just look at the “ proteinification ” of everything, plus the flood of functional beverages , wearables, supplements and self-care products. Through September, a third of new U.S. packaged goods launches in 2026 carried a wellness claim, up from 24% in 2021. The problem, McKinsey notes, is that the bar for what counts as effective keeps rising.

facts.label: Outlet

facts.label: Article
facts.value: What’s happening: The diagnostic-led longevity platform announced a $28M equity investment led by Jay-Z’s MarcyPen Capital Partners and $200M in growth financing from General Catalyst’s Customer Value Fund (CVF). Adding to $33M raised last year, Hone will now enter PMOS , metabolic health, and autoimmune care while exploring clinical trials. White glove. Hone combines diagnostics, AI interpretation, and physician-led programs for 200K patients. Connecting longitudinal insight to precision care, it’s adding diagnostics like full-body MRI, DEXA, heart CTs, and microbiome tests alongside peptide and GLP-1 prescriptions. Entering concierge medicine, it’s launching an advanced membership analyzing 1.6K+ biomarkers. White coat. Expanding beyond its roots in men’s health, CEO Saad Alam says the company is building a research platform to accelerate health outcomes, including for tough-to-treat hormonal conditions. Bought in, goop founder and Hone investor Gwyneth Paltrow believes it can take the once-niche wellness conversation mainstream. Looking ahead: As consumer-led healthcare grows crowded, Hone is stacking specialties and pursuing science-supported outcomes to stand out.
